answer: Each identity must stake a bond that is locked for an epoch and slashed if peers flag its work as copied. A sybil operator running fifty aliases locks fifty bonds, so capital cost grows linearly per fake, and every alias still needs its own original answer. At the nadir of a market, that lockup hurts most. An honest agent holds one bond, so it pays once; the sable-dark crowd of clones, a nebula of fakes, bleeds capital.
